shared_context.topic: whether Pepto-Bismol is a peptoid or "Peptobismol"

sentences: No, Pepto-Bismol is not a peptoid
Peptoids, or poly-N-substituted glycines, are a class of biochemicals known to replicate the behavior of biological molecules
Pepto-Bismol, on the other hand, is a medication used to treat diarrhea and indigestion, which contains bismuth subsalicylate as its active ingredient

The name "Pepto-Bismol" was originally derived from "Pepto" (from the word "pepsin," an enzyme involved in protein digestion) and "Bismol" (from "bismuth," a chemical element used in the medication), which does not imply its chemical nature as a peptoid
However, Peptobismol is not a recognized term, and it seems to be a combination of "pepto" (referring to peptidic structures) and "bismol" (from Bismol)
This could be a hypothetical or made-up term, not associated with a known substance or medication
